source: User-provided auth-flow-studio-expansion-worker-plan.html, 21 October 2026. These requirements are extracted from the plan, not generated by a runtime model builder.
negativeVariants: Named variants are required tests, not additional catalog entries.
manualG01: Explicitly open by user decision. No screen-reader speech/comprehension or overall manual acceptance pass is claimed.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Domain account; S’s machine secure channel ready; NTLMv2 permitted. C, S, D.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: NEGOTIATE, CHALLENGE, AUTHENTICATE; S requests DC validation and receives its result; S completes context and application authorization. Sending AUTHENTICATE is not success.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Explicit S-local account, valid local credential record, allowed logon. C, S/local authority.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: The same challenge-response family validates against S’s local account database. No DC query, Kerberos ticket or implicit domain lookup appears.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Resource domain trusts account domain; declared direct trust and healthy channels. C, S, DR, D.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: S→DR→D validation and reverse result delivery; S authorizes the resource. Display trust direction separately from request direction. This covers NTLM trust traversal independently of Kerberos referrals.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Same topology; selected trust-routing/name-validation prerequisite fails. C, S, DR, D as applicable.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Terminate at the actual failing routing/validation authority; return failure through existing hops. No invented successful remote validation, context, ticket or resource access.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: W01 with a response inconsistent with the supplied challenge/credential context.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: DC rejects the response, S receives failure, client receives its carrier-specific failure. Preserve the distinct “server knows failure” and “client learns failure” moments.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Working SPN, service key, client credentials and Kerberos policy. C, S, D/KDC.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Negotiate selects Kerberos; show ticket acquisition/context establishment and subsequent service authorization. Explain the wrapper, selected mechanism and carrier separately.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Explicit supported condition selecting NTLM; both peers/policies permit it. C, S, D.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Record the selection reason, then execute W01’s NTLMv2 exchange. Do not model every Kerberos error as an automatic fallback trigger.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: W07 selection condition; one named client/server/domain NTLM restriction applies.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Stop at that policy’s documented enforcement point. Preserve any earlier transport/negotiation state; create no authenticated context or successful application result.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: CredSSP v6 peers; trusted target under declared policy; Kerberos and delegation allowed. C, H, KDC.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Inner TLS, Kerberos via SPNEGO, directional binding verification, protected password-credential transfer. End at H’s receipt/recovery of delegated credentials; show local logon as a distinct operation.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Explicit NTLMv2 CredSSP profile and server-authentication/delegation assumptions. C, H, D.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Reuse CredSSP’s outer stages with NTLMv2 inside. Show DC validation where applicable and an NTLM session key, not a Kerberos subsession key.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Established TLS and mechanism context; incorrect server-to-client binding proof.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: C verifies and rejects the received proof before sending authInfo. No delegated password reaches H and no remote logon follows.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Credentials available locally; target is outside the selected delegation policy.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Policy denies export at its verified implementation point. No authInfo containing user credentials is sent. Do not unnecessarily force preceding handshakes if the client rejects earlier.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: W09 completes credential delivery; target’s selected remote-logon right/policy denies access.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: H has received credentials but creates no successful remote session. Communicate denial without erasing already completed credential exposure/history.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Ordinary password CredSSP/NLA; permitted remote logon and downstream ACL. C, H, D, R.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: RDP security negotiation, W09, remote authorization/session, then a separate H→R authentication/access as the user. Remote desktop readiness follows the selected RDP completion boundary.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Mode requested/supported, eligible administrator, permitted policy. C, H, D, R.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Credential-less logon with empty password-credential structure, then downstream access using H’s identity. Use a declared host-authorized resource so the identity difference is visible.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Direct supported RDP connection, AD target, Kerberos available, redirected authentication supported. C, H, D, R.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Redirected credentials and required MS-RDPEAR operations; remote session; downstream user SSO. Long-term user secrets remain at C; do not deny H’s legitimate service-ticket holdings.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Remote Credential Guard explicitly required; Kerberos cannot be established.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Fail with a mechanism/prerequisite explanation. No NTLM fallback, ordinary credential delegation or silent change to Restricted Admin.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Selected Restricted Admin or Remote Credential Guard requirement; target lacks corresponding support.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Reject at documented RDP negotiation/policy boundary. Parameterized fixtures verify both modes; neither becomes an ordinary password logon.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Normal nondelegating first-hop session; no RunAs, alternate credentials or other delegation solution. C, H, D, R.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: First hop succeeds; H cannot authenticate to the chosen second-hop file resource as the user. First-hop session remains valid after downstream denial.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Explicit credentials; client/service CredSSP enabled; target allowed; HTTPS profile; downstream user permitted.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Show outer HTTPS separately, complete inner CredSSP and H’s authorized WinRM session, then new H→R authentication and resource access using delegated credentials.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Explicit credentials; client delegation target not permitted, or a separately named credential-protection restriction applies.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Deny before exporting credentials; no privileged WinRM session or second hop follows. Do not relabel this as an incorrect password.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: W20’s authorized policy using an HTTP listener; Kerberos-based target authentication; verified HTTP/CredSSP profile.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Explain absence of outer HTTPS while retaining CredSSP’s inner TLS and applicable message protection. Credentials never become plaintext HTTP header values.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: W20 with successful second-hop authentication but R’s resource ACL denying the user.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Second-hop identity is established; resource authorization fails. Keep first-hop authentication, delegated-credential receipt and second-hop context distinct and intact.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: RADIUS password accept. Explicit PAP-style User-Password profile; user entry at the NAS is a declared local input. NAS sends Access-Request; server validates credentials and policy; Access-Accept returns authorization attributes.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: NAS verifies and applies the reply before its service becomes active. No browser session, OAuth token or Kerberos ticket is created.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: RADIUS password reject. Same profile and initial holdings, with an invalid password. Request reaches the server and receives Access-Reject.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: No authorized NAS session is created. Keep an authentication rejection distinct from a timeout or discarded invalid packet.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Password plus TOTP challenge. An explicitly illustrative server policy combines a password check with an Access-Challenge prompting for a TOTP response. NAS returns the server's opaque State unchanged in the next Access-Request.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Only successful second-factor and policy checks lead to acceptance. The RADIUS standard supplies messages, not a universal MFA workflow.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Challenge failure. Pair with NET-R03 using an invalid/expired synthetic TOTP. Show the validator's decision and the resulting rejection.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Challenge context terminates according to declared policy. Altered or missing State is a separate negative test, with no invented generic protocol result.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Wired 802.1X, EAP-TLS 1.3. Initially unauthorized switch port; EAP identity exchange; Access-Request/Challenge rounds carrying EAP-TLS; certificate and Finished checks; protected success, EAP/RADIUS result, then port enforcement.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: The controlled port opens only after the accepted result is processed. State explicitly that this does not establish MACsec or prove Internet reachability.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Server-certificate rejection. The peer detects an untrusted issuer, wrong configured server identity, expired certificate or revoked certificate. Use named fixture variants with the failing check visible.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: No successful EAP completion or authorized port. Show the selected alert/failure propagation and label whether its protection is already established.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Client-certificate rejection. The EAP server rejects a bad chain, inappropriate certificate use or expired/revoked client credential.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: No authorization succeeds; possession of a private key alone is insufficient. The certificate private key never appears on a wire or at the NAS.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Valid identity, policy denied. Certificate authentication establishes identity, but the configured network-access policy rejects that identity or access context.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Show the policy decision before a successful EAP result; no success indicator or port opening is fabricated merely because cryptographic checks passed.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: NPS with AD DS. Windows Server 2022 NPS, Windows 11 24H2 peer, certificate-based EAP-TLS with TLS 1.2, configured AD account mapping and group-based network policy. Author a full authentication, not a resumed TLS 1.3 exchange.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Display this pinned implementation profile separately from NET-E01; record evidence and configured prerequisites before claiming product support.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: NPS account-mapping failure. A cryptographically valid certificate does not satisfy the profile's required account-binding rules.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: No mapped identity or authorized access is invented. Explain the distinction between certificate validity, account binding and policy membership.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Accounting lifecycle. An already established service sends Accounting-Request Start, configured Interim-Update records and Stop, each with its Accounting-Response.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: One stable session correlation, cumulative counters, separate delivery acknowledgements. A missing accounting reply does not automatically revoke network access.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Classic UDP versus RadSec. Paired playback of the same authentication policy over classic RADIUS/UDP and a named RADIUS/TLS profile. RadSec establishes its transport before carrying RADIUS.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Two TLS contexts remain distinguishable when the inner method is EAP-TLS. Ordinary RadSec does not silently become RADIUS/1.1.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: RadSec peer-identity failure. The transport peer fails its configured trust/identity check before application traffic is accepted.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: No RADIUS authentication or EAP result is inferred. Display transport failure, not invalid user credentials.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Realm-routed proxy success. NAS sends to a proxy; the configured realm route selects a home server. Requests and replies traverse distinct adjacent-peer associations.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Preserve routing metadata and per-hop validation. The proxy does not acquire the EAP-TLS session's decrypted private fields merely by forwarding it.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Unknown realm. The same proxy cannot find an allowed route; author a specific local reject policy.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: No home-server exchange is shown. State that this reply is the selected routing policy, not a universal required unknown-realm response.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: CoA acknowledged. A trusted dynamic-authorization client targets an existing NAS session and requests a supported filter change.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: NAS applies the change before CoA-ACK; sender learns success on ACK receipt. The existing session keeps its identity.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: CoA rejected. Request an unsupported service or target an absent session; return the applicable CoA-NAK and Error-Cause.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: The authored rejected operation causes no new effective policy. Do not treat the NAK as an Access-Reject for a new login.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Disconnect acknowledged. A trusted request identifies one existing session; NAS terminates it and clears its associated context.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Disconnect-ACK follows termination. Accounting Stop is a separate subsequent event; no unrelated sessions disappear.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Disconnect rejected. Use a session-not-found fixture and return Disconnect-NAK with the matching error.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: An unrelated active session remains unchanged. Sender timeout and recipient rejection remain different states.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Lost reply and duplicate request. Drop a selected UDP response, show a timed NAS retry and the server's cached response to the valid duplicate.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: The logical authentication/session is processed once. Retransmission is another wire occurrence, not a second successful login.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Enterprise Wi-Fi, bounded EAP lesson. Substitute a pass-through AP and show the EAP authentication/access decision with appropriate key-material ownership.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: End with EAP access decision complete; Wi-Fi link establishment not shown. Never label encrypted Wi-Fi usable in this bounded scenario.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Experimental RADIUS/1.1. Two explicitly capable peers negotiate the RFC 9765 profile over TLS or DTLS; replay a small existing authentication example.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Use the profile's packet rules and removed MD5/shared-secret semantics. No automatic upgrade of an existing UDP path or NPS support claim.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Required RADIUS/1.1 unavailable. A strict configured peer does not obtain an acceptable negotiated profile.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Stop the connection according to that profile; do not silently fall back to an unprotected transport or report bad user credentials.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Compatible groups and correct password; ordinary negotiation.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Complete initial authentication, then obtain a service ticket and perform a service exchange. Distinguish ticket receipt, successful use and any established application session.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Client input differs from the provisioned secret; timestamp fallback disabled.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Failed verification, no accepted AS reply and no usable TGT. Existing unrelated state must remain unchanged.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Disjoint configured groups; authored KDC policy chooses rejection.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Negotiation failure without manufacturing a shared key. Explain that this preset fixes the rejection policy rather than asserting that every KDC must take this branch immediately.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Attacker suppresses initial SPAKE advertisement; timestamp fallback is permitted.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Clearly named fallback exchange and reduced protection. Any resulting TGT is attributed to that exchange, never to successful SPAKE.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Same interference, with timestamp fallback disabled.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Authentication stops. Show the exact policy decision and absence of a usable credential.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: KDC proposes a supported group in its first response.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Successful shorter exchange; identify the omitted negotiation round trip in comparison mode.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Initial proposed group is unsupported, but another compatible group exists.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Return to support negotiation, reset the transcript branch correctly, then succeed.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Client sends its support information in the initial request.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Successful alternate entry path, with required key-derivation inputs available before their first use.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Show the setup prerequisite, public exchange, independent derivations and both confirmation checks; finish with endpoint-specific confirmed-key state.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Show the setup prerequisite, public exchange, independent derivations and both confirmation checks; finish with endpoint-specific confirmed-key state.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Different inputs produce a failed confirmation. Do not mark a derived candidate key usable merely because local computation completed.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Different inputs produce a failed confirmation. Do not mark a derived candidate key usable merely because local computation completed.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: A fixed identity/transcript mismatch reaches a named verification failure. Identify the changed field and the rejecting endpoint.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: A fixed identity/transcript mismatch reaches a named verification failure. Identify the changed field and the rejecting endpoint.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Include registration as an explicitly declared setup phase, show the stored verifier record, then authenticate and confirm before the final shared-key state.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Include registration as an explicitly declared setup phase, show the stored verifier record, then authenticate and confirm before the final shared-key state.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Retain the legitimate stored record while the supplied password differs; show rejection and temporary-state cleanup.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Retain the legitimate stored record while the supplied password differs; show rejection and temporary-state cleanup.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Use a fixed context/identity mismatch; no authenticated application exchange follows failed confirmation.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Use a fixed context/identity mismatch; no authenticated application exchange follows failed confirmation.

scenarios.prerequisiteOrLesson: Compare client and server stored objects before and after an explicitly labelled teaching-only record-disclosure event. Explain what the record enables and what still requires recovering a password. Do not turn this into an exploit tool.
scenarios.requiredTerminalBoundary: Compare client and server stored objects before and after an explicitly labelled teaching-only record-disclosure event. Explain what the record enables and what still requires recovering a password. Do not turn this into an exploit tool.
